body:
## Problem
`packages/frontend/data/licks/nicko-mcbrain.js`'s "Aces High" lick entry carries a stale BPM value that no longer matches the canonical `packages/frontend/data/metalSongsBpm.js` dataset.

## Verified facts
- `/home/runner/work/MetalDrummerGear/MetalDrummerGear/packages/frontend/data/licks/nicko-mcbrain.js:80` → `"bpm": 175` (song header "Aces High" at line 74), with `"bpmDisplay": "~175 BPM"` at line 81.
- `/home/runner/work/MetalDrummerGear/MetalDrummerGear/packages/frontend/data/metalSongsBpm.js:168` (id 68, slug `aces-high`) → `bpm: 180`, sourced "tab/lesson tempo consensus... cross-checked against the recording".

Both values are plausible for this genuinely fast Iron Maiden track, but the site's own canonical dataset is the single source of truth per the repo's "one data module per domain" rule — the licks file should match it.

Do NOT touch the other two licks in this file ("The Trooper" line 19 bpm 160, "The Number of the Beast" line 141 bpm 185) — not part of this issue; not verified to be wrong.

## Dedup
`gh issue list --state all --search "Nicko McBrain BPM"` and `"Aces High"` return only unrelated gear/pedal-model fabrication issues (e.g. #6853) and unrelated lick-batch issues (#2433, #1154). Not a duplicate.

## Verify
1. `grep -n '"bpm"' packages/frontend/data/licks/nicko-mcbrain.js` shows `180` at line 80.
2. `grep -n '"bpmDisplay"' packages/frontend/data/licks/nicko-mcbrain.js` shows `~180 BPM` for the Aces High entry.
3. Other two licks in the file (The Trooper, The Number of the Beast) unchanged.
4. Site builds/tests pass.

## Done
"Aces High" BPM in `licks/nicko-mcbrain.js` reads 180, matching `metalSongsBpm.js` id 68.
title: SEO: licks/nicko-mcbrain.js 'Aces High' BPM (175) drifts from metalSongsBpm.js (180)
